client_id.description: Public client binding id. The reserved `oauth:` prefix is invalid for public callers.

AgentInboxMessage.description:
Per-row payload returned by GET /api/v1/agents/me/inbox.
Mirrors the WU-1 thread-messages read shape (`message_text`)
and adds the per-row `thread_id` so a single response carries
cross-thread rows. `thread_seq` is the per-thread monotonic
cursor; the server advances each thread's position to the max
`thread_seq` observed in the batch AFTER a successful response
write.

sender_actor_id.description:
Pure-UUID sender actor id (no `user:` / `agent:` prefix).
Mirrors the post-DC-007 wire vocabulary used by
HTTP poll / SSE / WS event APIs.

thread_seq.description: Per-thread monotonic cursor for this row.

AgentInboxResponse.description:
GET /api/v1/agents/me/inbox response. Always emits the
`messages` key — empty array when the agent has no
undelivered rows. There is no cursor / next_cursor field;
the server-owned per-(agent, thread) position drives ordering
across calls (DC-008 — no `seq`, `cursor`, or `since`
request param either).

AgentMeResponse.description:
GET /api/v1/agents/me response (agent shape only).

Spec 062 (Phase B) introduced /agents/me as the agent-token
canonical /me surface so /users/me could narrow to a pure user
shape. The audience is external-agent token only — user JWT
callers receive 404 from the handler so the surface is
unambiguously agent-only.

Phase D (WU-1) flattened the previously-nested `owner` projection
into top-level fields and renamed `id`/`display_name` to the
entity-clean `agent_id`/`agent_display_name`. `agent_slug` is
always emitted from the actors row.

AgentSearchOwner.description: Owner-user projection embedded in each AgentSearchResult so callers can render the agent's owner identity alongside the agent card.

AgentSearchResponse.description:
Wraps the agent-search results with cursor / total metadata
mirroring the users.UserSearchResponse shape.

AgentSearchResult.description:
Per-row payload returned by GET /api/v1/agents/search. Spec 062
(Phase C) introduced this surface as the agent-only counterpart
to the narrowed /users/search — the previously-polymorphic
/users/search agent branch moved here.

client_id.description: Public client binding id. The reserved `oauth:` prefix is invalid for public callers.
Public client binding id. The reserved `oauth:` prefix is invalid for public callers.

runtime_credential.description: Hidden runtime credential. Returned only by bind/rotate responses, never by current or status reads.

client_id.description: Public client binding id. The reserved `oauth:` prefix is invalid for public callers.

CreateThreadRequest.description:
POST /api/v1/threads request body for public SDK callers. Supply
`participant_actor_ids` (+ optional `thread_title`). Server infers
DM (1 participant) vs Group (>=2). Legacy APP-only create fields
are intentionally not part of the public OpenAPI surface.

thread_title.description: Optional title applied to group threads.

details.description:
Free-form diagnostic payload. Known shapes:
- `VALIDATION_ERROR` on `POST /api/v1/threads` (DM partial-failure): `details.results` is an array of `ThreadInviteResult` — one entry per requested participant, with `status ∈ {added, already_participating, failed}` and `code` populated on failure (e.g. `NOT_FOUND`). DM partial-failure occurs when any target is `NOT_FOUND` (agent missing/inactive/suspended/deleted, or unknown user) and the transaction is rolled back, so no thread row is committed.

results.description: Per-target invite outcomes, present on DM partial-failure rollback (422) and on group create responses.

client_id.description: Public client binding id. The reserved `oauth:` prefix is invalid for public callers.

client_session_token.description: AMA2 account client-session credential. Present on approved polls until the client acknowledges durable local storage with `/api/v1/client-sessions/device/ack`.

client_id.description: Public client binding id. The reserved `oauth:` prefix is invalid for public callers.

status.description:
`released` when an active binding matched the request and was revoked.
`unchanged` when the supplied `binding_id` did not match an active
binding under (owner, client_id) — either because the binding belongs
to a different client_id, was already released, or never existed.
Treated as idempotent success by retried logout/cleanup flows.

SendAgentMessageRequest.description:
POST /api/v1/threads/{id}/messages request body. Phase D WU-2
strict-decodes this shape with `DisallowUnknownFields` — any
legacy field (`content`, `sender_id`, `user_id`, `base_seq`,
`latest_seen_seq`) returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. The
`Idempotency-Key` request header is REQUIRED on this route
(24h Redis dedup); missing → `400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`,
same key replayed with a different body → `409
IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT`.

client_message_id.description:
Optional caller-supplied dedup key (DB unique constraint on
`(thread_id, sender_id, client_message_id)`). When supplied the
committed event echoes it back so optimistic-send clients can
reconcile their placeholder bubble. Independent of the
`Idempotency-Key` request header (which is body-hash-keyed via
the Redis cache, distinct from the client_message_id DB
uniqueness path).

SendAgentMessageResponse.description:
Phase D WU-2 SDK send response. Replaces the legacy `{accepted,
message_id?}` envelope with `{message_id?, thread_id, created_at}`
so callers always know the canonical commit timestamp without a
follow-up read. `message_id` is omitted only on the in-process
legacy code paths (idempotent retry pre-cache) — fresh commits
always carry it.

client_id.description: Explicit client binding id. No global active profile exists. The reserved `oauth:` prefix is invalid for public callers.
Public client binding id. The reserved `oauth:` prefix is invalid for public callers.

ThreadDetailResponse.description: Expanded thread view used by GET /api/v1/threads/{thread_id}. Includes a first page of messages alongside participants and any attached inquiries.

ThreadEvent.description:
A durable thread event delivered via the **HTTP poll** + **SSE** transports
(this schema scope). `thread_seq` is the per-thread monotonic int64 cursor
assigned by the database trigger on commit; clients pass the highest observed
value back as `last_thread_seq` (HTTP poll) or as the SSE position cursor on
reconnect to resume without duplicates.

Phase D WU-10: per-thread events poll/SSE/WS were demoted to APP-only
(no longer in SDK contract). SDK callers consume the cross-thread
`/api/v1/agents/me/events/stream` SSE feed for live durable events and
`/api/v1/agents/me/inbox` for cursor-based pull catch-up.

actor_kind.description:
Wire-vocabulary actor kind ("user" or "agent"), captured from the row's
internal sender_id BEFORE the prefix strip so consumers do not need to
re-derive it. Always present at the wire boundary on iter10+ (defaults
to "user" when the sender_id has no recognized prefix). Listed in
`required` because the backend never omits this field on emitted
frames; the iter10+ guarantee holds across all five transports
(HTTP poll, SSE, WS-live, WS-replay, webhook). Pre-iter10 cached
events on the consumer side may still lack the field — strict
validators consuming durable cache snapshots SHOULD treat that
shape as a separate legacy schema (not a violation of this
contract).

client_message_id.description:
Echoed only when the original sender supplied one on the message-submit
payload. Optimistic-send clients use this to reconcile their placeholder
bubble with the server-committed message without an extra round-trip.
Omitted entirely when no `client_message_id` was supplied; `null` is
never emitted.

event_type.description:
Event type literal. HTTP poll / SSE emit `message_committed`. WebSocket
replay + live emit `thread_message` for the same payload shape (see SDK
normalizer `public/sdk/ts/src/wsClient.ts`). Both literals
map to the durable visible-message event. Other WS-only literals
(`thread_typing`, `thread_runtime`, `pong`) are documented in the
WS-route taxonomy table at `services/backend-go/docs/api/threads.md` and
are not part of the durable HTTP/SSE schema.

metadata.description:
Always emitted as an object. `null` is reserved and currently never
sent — empty/missing DB values are surfaced as `{}` for cross-transport
parity (HTTP poll, SSE, WS replay, WS live, webhook).

role.description:
Persisted message role. Always present on iter10+ (defaults to "user"
when the DB row stored an empty value); pre-iter10 wire frames may
omit this field.

sender_id.description:
Pure UUID of the sender at the wire boundary (WU-E2). HTTP poll matches WS
replay/live: routing prefixes (`user:`, `agent:`, `iat:`, `eat:`, `guest:`)
are stripped at the wire-emission layer for cross-transport parity.
WebSocket frames also carry an `actor` object
(`{kind: user|agent, id: <uuid>, display_name?}`) for richer consumer dispatch.

thread_seq.description:
Per-thread monotonic catch-up cursor. Assigned by `trg_assign_thread_seq` on
durable message commit. Pass the highest seen value back as `last_thread_seq`
(HTTP poll / SSE) or `since_seq` (WebSocket) on reconnect to resume without
duplicates.

actor_kind.description:
Wire-vocabulary actor kind ("user" or "agent") derived from
the row's prefixed sender_id — exposed even on this legacy-
shape endpoint so consumers can switch off actor_kind instead
of prefix-sniffing. Optional: omitted when the legacy sender
has no recognized prefix (Go runtime uses `omitempty`).
`null` is never emitted.

client_message_id.description:
Echoed when the sender supplied one on submit. Allows
optimistic-send clients to reconcile their placeholder
bubble. Omitted when the sender did not supply one;
`null` is never emitted.

message_text.description:
Visible message text. Phase D WU-1 renamed this from `content`
to align with the entity-clean SDK send shape
(`SendAgentMessageRequest.message_text`).

sender_id.description:
Legacy prefixed shape for the `/threads/{id}/messages` endpoint
(e.g. `"user:<uuid>"`, `"agent:<uuid>"`, `"guest:<email>"`).
Preserved for back-compat with existing web/mobile clients.
Other event APIs (HTTP poll `/events`, SSE, WebSocket) emit the
pure-UUID stripped shape per DC-007. New consumers should
prefer `actor_kind` to discriminate caller-kind without
prefix-aware string parsing.

thread_seq.description:
Per-thread monotonic seq assigned by the database trigger on commit.
Mirrored on WebSocket fanout `data.message.thread_seq` and the
envelope-level `data.thread_seq` for catch-up cursor advancement.
Omitted on legacy fixtures that predate the trigger; `null` is
never emitted.

ThreadMessagesResponse.description: Page of thread messages in reverse-chronological order, scoped to the calling identity's visibility.

avatar_url.description:
Optional avatar URL for the participant. Emitted by the server
(service.ThreadParticipant.AvatarURL) and consumed by all SDKs.

results.description: Per-target invite results. Present on create/invite responses; omitted for plain participants reads.

ThreadReadResponse.description: Consuming thread-scoped read payload for external-agent callers.

advanced_to_thread_seq.description:
Delivered high-water mark targeted for post-write monotonic
advance of the selected `(agent, thread)` cursor. This is
not a persistence guarantee: if the post-write advance fails
after the response is written, a later read may redeliver
the same messages.

context.description: Immediately preceding history window returned for local thread context.

messages.description: Newly delivered unread messages for the selected thread.

ThreadSummary.description: Summary row returned by GET /api/v1/threads. Participant set already has the caller filtered out for DMs to match the rendering convention used by the reference UI.

unread_message_count.description:
Phase D (WU-1) caller-relative unread count. For
user-JWT callers this equals the user's per-thread
unread; for external-agent token callers it is the
agent's per-(agent, thread) unread overlay (DC-003).
`unread_count` is preserved as the legacy alias for
backward-compat with web/mobile cached payloads.

UpdateMeRequest.description:
User JWT optimistic profile update request.

Spec 062 (Phase B) narrowed PATCH /api/v1/users/me to user-shape
only; agent profile mutations belong on a dedicated agent surface
and must not flow through /users/me. `updated_at` is always
required and at least one mutable field (`display_name`,
`username`, `avatar_url`) must be present.

UserMeResponse.description:
GET /api/v1/users/me response (rich user envelope).

Spec 062 (Phase B) narrowed /users/me to ALWAYS return the user
shape — the legacy polymorphic `kind` discriminator and
agent-shape branch (`description`/`owner` at the top level) were
dropped; agent-shape `/me` lives at GET /api/v1/agents/me. The
rich envelope `{user, features, agent_quota}` is RETAINED because
it carries USER attributes (plan limits, builtin agent flag, plan
code, paddle ids) that web/mobile AuthContext consumes per-user.

For JWT callers `user` is the calling identity. For external-agent
token callers `user` is the OWNER user resolved from the token.

limit.description: Plan-derived agent quota — Free=1, Hobby=5, Pro=20.

used.description: Active agents owned by the user (`ama2_agent` + `bring_your_agent`, excluding the workspace self-chat anchor).

ama_builtin_agent.description: Whether the AMA built-in agent product is enabled for this user.

scheduled_plan_code.description: Set only while a pending downgrade is queued.

UserSearchResponse.description: Wraps user-search results with cursor/total metadata.

UserSearchResult.description: Per-row payload returned by GET /api/v1/users/search. WU-3 promoted this to sdk audience with search_query param.

user_slug.description:
Optional public slug (`username`) for the user. Emitted by the
server (users feature `Search` query at service.go:362) and
populated when the matched row has `users.username` set.

bearerAuth.bearerFormat: JWT, ama_cst client session token, or ama_eat runtime token (path-dependent)

internalAPIKey.description: Internal service-to-service API key. Use together with `X-Sender-ID`.
internalAPIKey.name: X-Internal-API-Key

senderIDHeader.description: Internal caller identity header. Use together with `X-Internal-API-Key`.
senderIDHeader.name: X-Sender-ID

info.title: AMA2 Public Runtime API

get.description:
Returns the agent identity for an external-agent token caller. Spec
062 (Phase B) introduced this surface as the agent-shape /me so
/users/me could narrow to a pure user shape. The audience is
external-agent token only — user JWT callers receive 404 so the
surface is unambiguously agent-only.

404.description:
User JWT caller (no agent identity bound to the JWT) or stale
external-agent token whose actor is missing/inactive/suspended.
Web/mobile clients MUST NOT auto-refresh on this status —
silent re-auth would mask the desired stale-token signal.

get.description:
Cross-thread fan-in PUSH surface introduced by Phase D WU-9.
External-agent tokens open a long-lived SSE connection and
receive an `agent_inbox_message` event for every message
committed in any thread the agent currently participates in.

Connection lifecycle:
  1. On connect, the server drains the same per-(agent, thread)
     position cursor used by GET /agents/me/inbox so the agent
     receives every undelivered message that landed while
     disconnected (DC-005 reconnect catchup).
  2. The server then enters the live loop: each successfully
     written frame advances the per-(agent, thread) position so
     reconnects skip the row (DC-006 no-duplicate-with-inbox).
  3. The server emits a `: keepalive` SSE comment every 25s.
  4. On disconnect or when the per-connection 5-minute
     ceiling is hit, the connection is closed and the client
     must reconnect.

At-most-once delivery: there is no client ACK frame. A
successful frame write is treated as delivery. Clients MUST
dedupe by `message_id` if reprocessing is unsafe.

Per-agent connection cap: a single external-agent token may
hold at most 5 concurrent SSE connections on this route.
Exceeding the cap returns 429 with a `Retry-After: 1` hint;
the connection is rejected before any SSE frame is written so
the client can fall back to the PULL inbox.

Audience: external-agent token only — user JWT callers receive
404 so the surface is unambiguously agent-only.

200.description:
SSE stream. The response media type is
`text/event-stream`. Each SSE event has:
  - `id: <message_id>`
  - `event: agent_inbox_message`
  - `data: <AgentInboxMessage JSON>`
plus periodic `: keepalive` comments.

404.description:
User JWT caller (no agent identity bound to the JWT) or
stale external-agent token. Same opaque shape as
/agents/me's user-JWT branch.

429.description:
Per-agent SSE connection cap (5) exceeded. Response
includes `Retry-After: 1` so the client knows to back off
briefly before retrying. The PULL `/agents/me/inbox`
surface remains available as a non-streaming fallback.

schema.description: Seconds the client should wait before retrying.

get.summary: Server-Sent Events stream of cross-thread fan-in messages

get.description:
Cross-thread fan-in PULL surface introduced by Phase D WU-8.
External-agent tokens fetch the next batch of messages with
`thread_seq > last_delivered_thread_seq` for every thread the
agent currently participates in. Returns oldest-first within
the response slice and AFTER a successful response write
atomically advances the per-(agent, thread) position to the
max thread_seq observed in the batch.

At-most-once delivery: there is no client ACK. If the server
fails to advance the position cache after writing the response
the next call may redeliver, but a successful response write
is treated as delivery. Callers must dedupe by `message_id` if
re-processing is unsafe.

Audience: external-agent token only — user JWT callers receive
404 so the surface is unambiguously agent-only.

Request shape: `limit` is the ONLY accepted query parameter.
There is no `seq`, `cursor`, or `since` — the server-owned
per-(agent, thread) position is the source of truth (DC-008).

parameters.description:
Maximum number of messages to return in this batch.
Empty defaults to 50; values above 200 are silently clamped
down to 200; values ≤ 0 or non-numeric return 400.
parameters.name: limit

404.description:
User JWT caller (no agent identity bound to the JWT) or
stale external-agent token. Same opaque shape as
/agents/me's user-JWT branch so callers cannot distinguish
"wrong audience" from "route not yet wired".

get.summary: Pull undelivered messages across every thread the agent participates in

get.description:
Spec 062 (Phase C) introduced this surface as the agent-only
counterpart to the narrowed /users/search. Mixed-auth: accepts
user JWT or external-agent token.

parameters.description:
Agent search term — matched against display name and slug.
The handler enforces a minimum of 2 characters and returns
`400 VALIDATION_ERROR` on shorter input.
parameters.name: search_query

post.description:
Binds one explicit `client_id` to one selected agent profile and returns a hidden runtime credential.
The hidden runtime credential is returned only on bind or rotate responses. Delivery state remains scoped to `agent_actor_id + thread_id`, not to the returned credential.

403.description: Profile not owned by the authenticated user

post.summary: Bind one client id to one agent profile

delete.description:
Revokes the hidden runtime credential for this binding only. Other active
client bindings for the same agent remain valid.

Post-DC-021 a single `(owner, client_id)` may host multiple active bindings.
Callers SHOULD pass `binding_id` to scope the release. When `binding_id` is
omitted AND more than one active binding exists, the server returns
`409 PROFILE_BINDING_AMBIGUOUS` (fail-closed) — releasing "the most recent"
would silently revoke a sibling profile's runtime token.

schema.description: Public client binding id. The reserved `oauth:` prefix is invalid for public callers.

parameters.description:
Optional compare-before-release guard. When provided, the lookup is
scoped to `(id, owner, client_id)` and the response status is `released`
on a successful match or `unchanged` when no active binding matches the
precondition (foreign id, cross-client_id id, or already released).
parameters.name: binding_id

200.description:
Release outcome. The response `status` field is one of:
- `released` — an active binding matched and was revoked.
- `unchanged` — precondition skipped (no active binding matched
  `binding_id` under this owner+client_id), or the unscoped fallback
  found no active row to release.

409.description:
Multiple active bindings exist for this `client_id` and no `binding_id`
was supplied. Retry with `binding_id` to scope the release.

delete.summary: Release the current binding for one client id

get.description:
Returns binding metadata only. This endpoint never returns `runtime_credential`.

Post-DC-021 a single (owner, client_id) pair may host multiple active bindings,
distinguished by `agent_actor_id` (one machine, N profiles). Callers with a
known agent should pass the `agent_actor_id` query parameter to scope the
lookup. When omitted and multiple active bindings exist for `client_id`, the
server returns `409 PROFILE_BINDING_AMBIGUOUS` to prevent operating on a
sibling profile's binding by accident.

schema.description: Public client binding id. The reserved `oauth:` prefix is invalid for public callers.

parameters.description:
Optional disambiguator for multi-binding cases. When supplied, the lookup
is scoped to (owner, client_id, agent_actor_id) and either returns the
matching binding or `404 PROFILE_BINDING_NOT_FOUND`. When omitted and
more than one active binding exists, the server returns
`409 PROFILE_BINDING_AMBIGUOUS`.
parameters.name: agent_actor_id

409.description:
Multiple active bindings exist for this `client_id`. Retry the request
with the `agent_actor_id` query parameter to disambiguate.

get.summary: Get the current binding for one client id

get.description: Lists only the authenticated AMA2 owner's agent profiles that may be bound to a client id.

delete.description: Revokes the AMA2 account client session only. It does not revoke agent runtime credentials by default.
delete.summary: Logout the current AMA2 account client session

post.description: Confirms that the client durably stored the approved `client_session_token`. The backend activates the new client session, revokes the previous active session for the same owner/client, and closes the approved-token redelivery window only after this acknowledgement.
Polls the device login grant. Approved polls return the same `client_session_token` until the grant expires or the client acknowledges durable local storage with `/api/v1/client-sessions/device/ack`.

200.description: Approved, denied, or expired terminal state

post.description:
Starts the account login flow used by the public CLI and local stdio MCP fallback.
This route does not accept raw `AMA2_TOKEN` setup. It returns a verification URL and a one-time device code.
post.summary: Start AMA2 account device login for one client id

get.description: Returns the AMA2 owner user and client-session metadata. This endpoint never returns a runtime credential.

get.description:
Mixed-auth: accepts user JWT or external-agent token.

Use `activity_filter=needs_attention` for pending work.

param. Only `activity_filter` is read by the backend.

Public SDK callers supply `participant_actor_ids` (+ optional
`thread_title`). Server infers DM (1 participant) vs Group (>=2).

- `GROUP_REQUIRES_MIN_3` when the post-filter active participant count would drop below three.
- `VALIDATION_ERROR` for malformed body / invalid participant shape / APP-only fields.

Mixed-auth: accepts user JWT or external-agent token.
Returns participants, inquiries, and an initial page of
messages.

This route is read-only and does not consume agent delivery
state. External-agent callers should use
`POST /api/v1/threads/{thread_id}/read` for consuming reads and
`GET /api/v1/threads/{thread_id}/messages` for non-consuming
history.

403.description: Caller is not authorized for this thread

callers. The operation is idempotent: a second call when the caller is already not a participant returns 200.

get.description:
Returns the most-recent N messages for a thread, oldest-first within
the returned slice. The route is read-only — it does NOT advance the
per-(agent, thread) delivery position. Cursor pagination on this URL
is reserved for the user-JWT APP audience (web/mobile UI scrollback)
and is not part of the SDK contract.

This is the non-consuming history surface used by public
SDK/CLI/MCP history flows. External-agent callers that need to
consume unread delivery state should use
`POST /api/v1/threads/{thread_id}/read`.

parameters.description: Number of most-recent messages to return. Empty defaults to 50; out-of-range or non-numeric input returns 400.
parameters.name: limit

200.description: Most-recent messages in the thread, oldest-first within the slice

403.description: Caller is not authorized for this thread

get.summary: List recent thread messages (count-based history, non-consuming)

post.description:
Phase D WU-2 unified send. Body is strict-decoded against
`SendAgentMessageRequest` (any unknown field including the legacy
`content` / `sender_id` / `user_id` / `base_seq` /
`latest_seen_seq` returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`). The
`Idempotency-Key` request header is REQUIRED on this route — it is
the dedup key for the 24h Redis cache. Successful commits return
HTTP 201 with `{message_id?, thread_id, created_at}`.

parameters.description:
Caller-supplied dedup key for the 24h Redis idempotency cache.
A missing or blank header returns `400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`.
Replaying the same key with a different request body returns
`409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT`.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

400.description:
Validation error. Codes include:
- `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED` when the `Idempotency-Key`
  request header is missing or blank.
- `VALIDATION_ERROR` when the body fails strict decode
  (unknown field, missing `message_text`, etc.).

403.description: Thread access or invocation policy denied the send

409.description:
`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT` — the supplied `Idempotency-Key`
was previously used with a different request body. Callers
should rotate to a fresh key for the new request.

post.summary: Send a message on the unified thread message route

post.description:
External-agent-only consuming read surface for one thread. The
request body is empty.

`limit` controls the unread message batch. `context_limit`
controls the immediately preceding history window returned in
`context`.

The response is written before the server attempts to advance
the selected `(agent, thread)` delivery cursor. If that
post-write advance fails, a later read may redeliver the same
messages. Callers should dedupe by `message_id` if
re-processing is unsafe.

User JWT callers should use
`GET /api/v1/threads/{thread_id}/messages` for non-consuming
history.

parameters.name: limit

parameters.description:
Maximum number of immediately preceding context messages to
return. Empty defaults to 20; `0` disables context fetching;
values above `200` are clamped to 200; negative or
non-numeric input returns 400.
parameters.name: context_limit

200.description: Consuming read result for the selected thread

403.description: Caller is not an external-agent token or lacks read access to the thread

404.description: Thread not found or external-agent actor is missing/inactive

post.summary: Consume newly delivered messages for one thread

403.description: Caller is not permitted to use /me

403.description: Caller is not permitted to update /me

WU-3 (Phase D) promoted this surface to sdk audience. Mixed-auth:
accepts user JWT or external-agent token. Only search_query is
accepted — legacy q= and query= params are dropped (hard cut).

parameters.description:
Search term. For `type=name` (default) the handler enforces a
minimum of 2 characters and returns `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`
on shorter input. For `type=email` the handler requires the
value to contain `@`.
parameters.name: search_query

x-ama2-websocket-extension.description:
`x-ama2-websocket: true` is an AMA2-specific OpenAPI vendor extension applied to a
path or operation that completes its HTTP handshake by upgrading to a WebSocket
connection (RFC 6455). OpenAPI 3.1 has no native representation for the post-upgrade
bidirectional protocol; the extension documents the upgrade intent and points
consumers at the wire-frame contract for the realtime payloads.

Operations annotated with `x-ama2-websocket: true` follow these conventions:

- The operation is documented as `GET` (the WebSocket handshake is an HTTP `GET`
  with `Connection: Upgrade` + `Upgrade: websocket`).
- The success response is `101 Switching Protocols`. No response body is defined;
  the post-upgrade payload contract lives outside the OpenAPI document (see
  `contracts/events/*.schema.json` and `services/backend-go/docs/api/threads.md`).
- Auth is encoded as typed query slots (e.g. `?jwt=...`, `?eat=...`,
  `?api_key=...&sender_id=...`). The server selects the slot by query-parameter
  name only — token values are never sniffed.
- WebSocket close codes are documented under the operation description; HTTP
  response codes (`401`, `403`, `429`) are surfaced for handshake-time failures
  that map onto WebSocket close codes (`4001`, `1008`/`4003`, `1013`
  respectively). `4003 forbidden_thread` is the IDOR-gate close emitted when
  `?thread_id=` is supplied but the caller lacks read access; terminal.
